decision: Build a human governance console at quorum serve /app (Phase 1: Proposal Review UI — browse, approve, reject, edit pending proposals with evidence inline). Extend quorum serve rather than adding new entry commands. MCP resource layer (quorum://chronicle/*, quorum://growth, quorum://sentinel/coverage, quorum://compass/map) for agent context. quorum_commit_proposal MCP tool must not auto-commit — it returns a proposal ID; the only commit paths are quorum commit <id> CLI or the UI approve button. Phase 2 (Chronicle browser + Growth dashboard) and Phase 3 (Sentinel + Compass maps) gate on Phase 1 usage evidence. Phase 4 (MCP Apps embedded widgets) is a research item, not roadmap.
key_insight: The governance UI closes the biggest UX gap in Quorum: the human-gate principle is validated across Chronicle, but reviewing raw JSON proposals in .chronicle/proposals/ is friction that deters real use. Proposal Review UI directly strengthens the most important Quorum invariant — humans approve memory — without weakening it. Agents stage; humans commit. This boundary must hold across CLI, MCP, and UI.
alternatives_considered: quorum mcp --ui as separate command from quorum serve
quorum_commit_proposal as an auto-committing MCP tool
MCP Apps (embedded UI widgets) as Phase 1 priority
Full dashboard (all pages) as v1 scope
rejected_reason: Separate serve/mcp commands duplicate the server entrypoint — quorum serve already exists and is the right extension point
Auto-committing MCP tool violates the agents-stage-humans-commit invariant; prompt-level guardrails are not security
MCP Apps spec is immature and depends on third-party host rendering support; risk outweighs reward in Phase 1
Full dashboard as v1 risks shipping nothing — Proposal Review alone has the highest ROI and lowest scope

conditions: quorum_commit_proposal MCP tool must not auto-commit — return proposal ID only
Phase 1 (Proposal Review UI) ships as v1; Phases 2-3 are v2; Phase 4 (MCP Apps) is research
quorum serve is the single entrypoint — no new top-level commands for starting the server

risks: UI becomes substitute for good agent prompting rather than complement
MCP Apps spec immaturity creates Phase 4 long-tail dependency
